daily_brief: The day's most consequential development is Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's formal rejection of President Trump's 15-point Gaza peace plan, a move that complicates US-led diplomacy in the region and raises questions about the future of the ceasefire framework [BBC], [RFI], [Le Monde]. Meanwhile, tensions between Iran and the United States persist, with Tehran conditioning the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz on the lifting of sanctions, compensation, and an end to military threats [France 24], [The Hindu]. In Europe, Germany is grappling with what officials describe as 'hybrid warfare,' following drone sightings over a military base housing Patriot missile components days after an explosive-laden device was found at Leipzig airport [BBC]. A diplomatic spat between Spain and Italy has escalated into mutual border controls, triggered by the mass migration event in Ceuta late last month, testing EU solidarity [The Guardian], [BBC]. On the public health front, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now exceeded 4,000 confirmed cases, with officials warning the virus may be mutating and calling for an urgent scale-up of response efforts [The Guardian].

top_stories.headline: Netanyahu Rejects Trump's 15-Point Gaza Plan, Demands Full Hamas Disarmament Before Any Withdrawal
bullets: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally rejected the US-backed 15-point peace plan for Gaza at a cabinet meeting on Sunday, stating Israel will not withdraw forces until Hamas is 'genuinely disarmed.'

Hamas had previously agreed to the plan, which included provisions for complete disarmament of armed groups in Gaza, though Hamas conditioned weapons handover on Israel ending 'all forms of aggression' and withdrawing.

The rejection marks a significant break between Netanyahu and President Trump, who had hailed the plan as a milestone for peace; Netanyahu described Trump as 'our greatest friend in the White House' but said Israel would stand its ground.
Oil prices rose following the announcement, with Brent crude gaining 0.6% to $84.04 per barrel.

top_stories.headline: Iran Sets Conditions for Reopening Strait of Hormuz, Including Sanctions Relief and Compensation
bullets: Iran's national security chief outlined demands the US must meet before Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, including lifting the naval blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damages, and release of frozen Iranian assets.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi said an agreement with Oman on new shipping lanes through the strait is in its 'final stages,' though broader reopening depends on US concessions.

President Trump indicated Washington is prioritizing economic pressure over new military strikes, citing Iran's financial difficulties and crediting the US naval blockade with deepening that pressure.
Trump noted oil prices have fallen to just above $75 per barrel, easing economic impact on American consumers.

sources.framing_note: Reported within Middle East live coverage, emphasizing regional shipping and security implications.

top_stories.headline: Germany Investigating Drone Incursions at Military Bases Amid 'Hybrid Warfare' Concerns
bullets: Two drones were spotted over a Bundeswehr base in Mechernich, near Bonn, on Thursday evening; the base reportedly houses components for US-made Patriot air-defense systems.
The incident comes days after an explosive-laden drone was found on a runway at Leipzig/Halle airport, which serves NATO, the German military, and Ukraine's Antonov Airlines.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt stated Germany has become a 'daily target of hybrid warfare,' though Moscow denies any involvement.
The Bundeswehr declined to comment on the suspected origins of the drones; local police are investigating.

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting with official statements; noted Moscow's denial of involvement.

top_stories.headline: Spain and Italy Impose Mutual Border Controls as Ceuta Migration Crisis Strains EU Relations
bullets: Spain imposed border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy starting at midnight Saturday, in response to Italy's earlier restrictions following an influx of approximately 78,000 migrants from Morocco into Ceuta on July 30-31.
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares described Italy's measures as 'a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity' and called them 'unfair, contrary to the EU's interests and discriminatory.'
Italy's government under Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni refused to revise its decision, stating checks would remain until at least August 15.
Spain stated that 5%-10% of passengers arriving from Italy would have their documents checked; both countries say their controls are random.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the political divide between Spain's socialist leader and Italy's conservative leader on migration policy.

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Focused on the procedural aspects and official statements from both governments.

top_stories.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 4,000 Cases as Officials Warn Virus May Be Mutating
bullets: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has exceeded 4,000 confirmed cases with at least 1,801 deaths as of early August.
Africa CDC Director General Dr. Jean Kaseya announced plans to scale up response efforts and go 'door to door' looking for patients, warning the time for incremental action was over.
Officials are conducting studies to determine whether the virus is mutating, citing the 'unprecedented' severity of the Bundibugyo outbreak.
The outbreak is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with eight times more cases and six times more deaths than were recorded 11 weeks into the 2014-18 West Africa outbreak.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the scale of the outbreak relative to historical precedents and quoted African health officials directly.
